title: IndiGo fares up 34% so why is it still losing money?

outro.text: Will fares fall when jet fuel is repriced on December 1? IndiGo fares up 34 percent, loss 1,879 crore rupees.

scenes.text: IndiGo fares up 34 percent, loss 1,879 crore rupees for July to September.
You're paying a third more per kilometre, and IndiGo is still losing money.
Fuel per passenger was 2,070 rupees a year ago, now 3,624 rupees.

card.title: Fuel per passenger
card.source: IndiGo Q2 FY27 press release (fuel cost ÷ passengers)

scenes.text: The rupee fell about 9 percent, jet fuel benchmark was up 60 percent.
Without currency effects loss was 7,237 million rupees, reported loss was 18,791 million.
Per passenger cost about 9,520 rupees, loss per passenger about 680 rupees.

funnel.long_title: Your IndiGo ticket costs more. So why is IndiGo still losing money?
